where: crates/blaze-scope/src/task/lower.rs (`rustc_builtin_macro` arm, `builtin_name`) and crates/blaze-scope/src/resolve.rs (the `MacroBody::BuiltinDerive` arm that picks `BuiltinDerive` by `mac.name`)
what: Writing a blaze-cli check test of a derive with a helper (the fixture shelf runs no proc macro and its core has no derive), I declared `#[rustc_builtin_macro(Copy, attributes(show))] pub macro Shown(..)`. The lowering reads the first argument into `builtin_name` and uses it to choose the shape, but `MacroBody::BuiltinDerive` keeps only the helpers, and the expansion picks the builtin by the macro's own name, so `Shown` would be `BuiltinUnknown`. The macro had to be named `Copy`.
cost: about ten minutes of reading before writing the test
cause: the builtin's name is read at lowering and not carried in the record's macro body
whys: `MacroBody::BuiltinDerive { helpers }` has no name field; the pinned library always names the macro as its builtin, so the gap never showed
class: a fact the lowering reads that the record drops, so two readers answer by different facts
prevention: carry the builtin's name in `MacroBody::BuiltinDerive` (and its record row) and pick by it, or refuse a `rustc_builtin_macro(Name, ..)` whose Name is not the macro's name, by name
workaround: name the macro as its builtin
